name: Intravesical gemcitabine + docetaxel (sequential, BCG-unresponsive NMIBC)
cyclesNote: Sequential same-visit intravesical gemcitabine then docetaxel, weekly for 6 weeks (induction), followed by monthly maintenance for responders. A bladder-sparing option for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC in patients declining or unfit for cystectomy.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Sequential intravesical gemcitabine + docetaxel is a salvage bladder-sparing regimen for BCG-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma. Cystectomy remains the preferred standard for fit patients. No molecular biomarker gates its use.

supportiveCare: Instill gemcitabine first (retain about 1-1.5 hours), have the patient void, then instill docetaxel (retain about 1-2 hours) at the same visit.
Confirm no active UTI or gross hematuria before each instillation.
Manage chemical cystitis symptomatically; disinfect voided urine per policy.
monitoring: cystoscopy + cytology at surveillance (about 3 months); low threshold to proceed to cystectomy

doseModificationRules.text: Hold instillations for severe local toxicity until recovery; consider dose/volume adjustment. Physician decides.

drugs.name: gemcitabine (intravesical)
drugs.notes: gemcitabine 1000 mg (commonly reconstituted in about 50-100 mL saline) instilled first and retained about 1-1.5 hours, then drained before docetaxel. A 2000 mg intravesical dose is an alternative. Own wording; standard reference dose.

provenance.locator: Principles of Intravesical Therapy - sequential gemcitabine/docetaxel

drugs.name: DOCEtaxel (intravesical)
drugs.notes: DOCEtaxel 37.5 mg (in about 50 mL saline) instilled after the gemcitabine dwell is drained, retained about 1-2 hours. ISMP tall-man DOCEtaxel (distinguish from PACLitaxel). Own wording; standard reference dose.

provenance.locator: Principles of Intravesical Therapy - sequential gemcitabine/docetaxel
